```{r libararies}
#general (from photosynthesis project, some might be unused)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r load data}
data <- read_csv("Data/TEMPEST_LeafSampleList_ISO_Ions_202605 - forR(SampleList).csv") |> 
  head(56) #kept returning 999 blank rows for some reason?
#i did cheat and manually add a plot column. seemed faster than trying to figure out the r verison

#get mean and sd for each isotope grouped by species and plot
grouped_data <- data |>
  group_by(Species, Plot) |>
  filter(!is.na(Br)) |> 
  mutate(
    mean_Br = mean(Br), 
    mean_Cl = mean(Cl),
    mean_NO3 = mean(NO3),
    mean_PO4 = mean(PO4),
    mean_SO4 = mean(SO4),
    sd_Br = sd(Br), 
    sd_Cl = sd(Cl),
    sd_NO3 = sd(NO3),
    sd_PO4 = sd(PO4),
    sd_SO4 = sd(SO4)
  )

```

```{r summarize ions: box plot}

#idea: box and whisker plots? (show range, which would be useful to know)
#can i cluster by plot but show by species? (yes! fill = does this)


#all appear mostly similar, minus a very wide range for saltwater litu
ggplot(grouped_data, aes(x = Plot, fill = Species, y = Br)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_bw()

#much higher in the saltwater plot, especially LITU! 
#control and fresh are all similar
#saltwater has a higher range, litu still is wayyyy higher
cl_box <- ggplot(grouped_data, aes(x = Plot, fill = Species, y = Cl)) +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Vegetation Campaign 2026 Leaf Cl", y = "Cl (mg/kg dw)") 
cl_box
ggsave(cl_box, filename = "graphs/Cl box plot (2026-10-02).jpg")

#not much difference across plots, it's more species-differences
#litu tends to be higher, fagr tends to be a but lower
ggplot(grouped_data, aes(x = Plot, fill = Species, y = NO3)) +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw()

#a bit of variation again, but mostly contained to litu
#beech runs mostly similar, acru is higher in freshwater and more in saltwater
#litu is similar control fresh but much higher salt
ggplot(grouped_data, aes(x = Plot, fill = Species, y = PO4)) +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw()

#nothing of note
ggplot(grouped_data, aes(x = Plot, fill = Species, y = SO4)) +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw()
```
